title: RandomizedSet: array + HashMap for O(1) insert/remove/getRandom.
shortTitle: RandomizedSet: array plus HashMap for O(1) insert, remove, getRandom
keyPoints: RandomizedSet combines a dynamic array for O(1) random indexing with a HashMap from element to index for O(1) lookup.
Insert appends to the array and records the index in the map; getRandom picks a random array index.
Remove swaps the target element with the last array element, updates the map for the moved element, then removes the last slot.
The swap-with-last trick avoids shifting, keeping removal O(1) and the array densely packed.
A densely packed array is what makes getRandom uniformly fair: every slot is occupied and equally likely.
Handle the edge case where the element being removed is already the last element to avoid map corruption.
All three operations run in average O(1) time.

s1_definition.oneliner: Store elements in an array for fair random indexing and keep a map from element to index, deleting by swapping with the last element so every operation stays constant time.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **RandomizedSet** – a data structure supporting insert, remove, and getRandom, all in average O(1) time.
- **Array** – stores elements for O(1) random indexing; `getRandom` picks a random index into this array.
- **HashMap** – maps each element to its current index in the array for O(1) lookup during insert and remove.
- **Swap-with-last removal** – move the last element into the vacated slot, update the map, and shrink the array. No shifting needed.
- **Dense packing** – the array has no holes, ensuring every index is equally likely in getRandom.
s1_definition.analogy: The National Bank of India runs a lucky-draw where every eligible account number must have an exactly equal chance of being picked, and accounts are added and removed from eligibility all day. A clerk keeps the account numbers in a numbered list for fair random picking, and a quick index card telling where each number sits. To remove an account fast, the clerk moves the last number into the removed slot and trims the list, so no gap is left.

sections.s6_takeaway:
A RandomizedSet supports insert, remove, and getRandom all in average O(1) time by combining a dynamic array with a HashMap. The array provides O(1) random access for fair random picks, and the map provides O(1) lookup of any element's position for fast removal.

The clever part is the swap-with-last removal technique. Instead of shifting elements (O(n)), you move the last element into the vacated slot, update the map for that moved element, and shrink the array. This keeps the array densely packed with no holes, which is exactly what makes getRandom uniformly fair.

The edge case to always handle is removing the element that is already last, where the swap is effectively a no-op but the map and array must still be updated consistently. Forgetting to update the map for the swapped element is the most common bug.

In a banking project at the National Bank of India, this structure powers a fair prize draw among eligible savings accounts, where eligibility changes continuously. The array never develops holes, so every draw gives each account exactly equal probability.

Remember one sentence: Combine an array for random indexing with a HashMap for O(1) lookup, and swap-with-last on remove to keep the array dense and all three operations O(1).
